title: Recent progress and challenges in Schiff base-based optical chemosensors
content: The traditional analytical methods for detecting environmentally or biologically important analytes are sensitive, but not suitable for rapid on-site analysis because they require complex instrumentation and laboratory facilities. Optical Schiff base-based chemosensors and biosensors are promising tools owing to their tunable photophysical properties, and colorimetry or fluorescence sensing modes. Recent literature on Schiff base-based optical chemosensors developed for the detection of environmental and biologically important analytes such as metal ions, toxic anions, environmental pollutants and clinically important biomolecules published from January 2020 to 31 July 2026 is critically reviewed. This review discusses structure–property relationships and sensing performance. In addition, important photophysical processes like intramolecular charge transfer (ICT), photoinduced electron transfer (PET), chelation-enhanced or chelation-quenched fluorescence (CHEF/CHEQ), excited-state intramolecular proton transfer (ESIPT), aggregation-induced emission (AIE), and analytical performance parameters, including sensitivity, selectivity, detection limits, linear ranges, response times, and applicability to real samples, were evaluated. Portability of novel sensing platforms, such as paper-based sensors, smartphone-assisted analysis, and nanomaterial-integrated sensors were specifically examined. Also, special attention was given to new approaches that combine molecular design with computational tools, chemometric data analysis, microfluidic devices and portable digital tools to enhance analytical performance and to increase applicability in real-world applications. Finally, the critical challenges and future perspectives of sustainable sensor design, novel sensing approaches using Internet of Things (IoT), Artificial Intelligence (AI), and Machine Learning (ML) for the future Schiff base-based optical sensors were surveyed.
